physicalNotes: Radius: Limb-darkened angular diameter 5.999 ± 0.025 mas measured with VLTI/PIONIER by Kervella et al. (2017), A&A 597, A137, who derive 0.8632 ± 0.0037 solar radii with the parallax 747.17 ± 0.61 mas. Adopted 600,528 km, 0.8632 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9092 ± 0.0025 solar masses from Akeson et al. (2021), AJ 162, 14 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.10086), from the orbit of Alpha Centauri A and B: gravitational parameter 120,662,150,486 km^3/s^2 at 132,712,440,041.94 km^3/s^2 per solar mass. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; no spin axis is adopted.

sources.distance: Inverse of the parallax 747.17 ± 0.61 mas that Kervella et al. (2017) adopt from Kervella et al. (2016)
sources.binary: Akeson et al. (2021), AJ 162, 14 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.10086) fit the orbit of Alpha Centauri A and B from astrometry and radial velocities and derive their masses, 1.0788 ± 0.0029 and 0.9092 ± 0.0025 solar masses: the pair is bound. This record adopts no orbit of the pair, so the star is placed by its own astrometry and carries no orbit.
